answer: Each bonded identity posts collateral, but equivocation proofs can link coordinated keys: for k identities, correlated offenses incur a penalty proportional to k², not k. Detection also applies a swarm-size exponential capital-loss multiplier, while asymmetric depreciation makes seized collateral harder to replace. Splitting stake across keys therefore does not dilute risk: a comet-like trail of signed conflicts may reveal the coordination spiral, even across a meadow of seemingly independent validators.
